$comment: ENGINE-WIDE defaults for per-story budgets. A project overrides any of these in its own llm-settings.json and need not restate the rest. These are the knobs an operator reaches for when a run burns its budget or a model truncates its answer — they were literals inside a case statement in a 10,000-line shell script, changeable only by editing code.

generator.description: a generator writes one large artefact in few turns — the inverse budget of an implementer

outputTokenFloors.$comment: Minimum output budget raised at specific steps that must not be truncated. Applied as a floor: the larger of the tier budget and this value wins.

$whyOutputCaps: Raised 2026-09-21 (regintel run 140717Z): medium/high were 6144, and z-ai/glm-5.3 returned exactly 6144 output tokens on every iteration of REGI-003b and REGI-004-A — truncated mid-answer, so the runner ended with no result (raw=0 bytes) and the ladder retried the identical cap seven times. A cap must leave a reasoning model comfortable room to finish an answer; 32768 is within every set's models' output limits.

timeouts.$comment: ENGINE-WIDE walls. A project overrides any of these in its own llm-settings.json; one that declares none inherits these, as with effortTiers. QUADRUPLED 2026-09-22 on the operator's instruction: the clock is not the pipeline's governance. What governs an attempt is its iteration budget, its deliverables gate and its review; the wall exists only to stop a hung process, so it sits far above the work rather than beside it. Before: an attempt floor of 3600s. REGI-003b died twice at 600s (the literal this block replaced) having read a 369-line file.

storyEffortTimeoutSecs.$comment: Per-effort floor for ONE attempt; the effective wall is derived from the attempt's own iteration budget (secondsPerIteration x maxIterations + perAttemptOverheadSecs) and capped at storyTimeoutMaxSecs. A floor exists so an attempt is never killed for being slower than the cheapest story in the phase.

timeouts.$whyEveryClock: Fourteen clocks were found on 2026-09-22; three were declared and the rest were literals at the point of use — one LLM call 240s, plan mode 90s, a tool call 15s, a commit 60s. The story wall was raised to four hours and two stories were still killed, because the wall is not the only clock. Every clock the engine applies is declared here, generously: the work is governed by iteration budgets, gates and review, never by time.

$whyCeilings: CEILINGS ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT RUNS ACTUALLY CONSUME, NOT AUTHORED. Raised 2026-09-23 from the regintel run's own usage traces (orchestrations/logs/usage-trace-<story>.jsonl, one line per model iteration): across 43 stories the iterations used ranged 9-120 with a median near 50, so 42 of 43 exceeded even the `max` tier of 20 — every tier was wrong by an order of magnitude, and runs completed only because each model override silently supplied 120-155 instead. Of 6,301 recorded iterations, 85 ended EXACTLY at a declared output ceiling (62 at the since-raised 6144, 12 at 8192, 7 at 12288, 3 at 16384, 1 at 32768) — an exact value repeating is a wall, not a model choosing to stop. THE RULE: a ceiling sits at no less than twice the largest legitimate observed use, and never below what the model's own override declares, so a ceiling can never be the thing that ends an attempt. generator.maxIterations 3 -> 12: a generator still reads before it writes.
